about: AdventureWorks workload for tools/sample_db_bench.py. origin 'upstream-view': the CREATE VIEW bodies of upstream/instawdb.sql (name = the upstream view name), adapted from T-SQL to BigQuery SQL as 'adaptation' says; 'upstream-procedure': the SELECT statements of the upstream functions and recursive stored procedures with their parameters bound to the values in 'adaptation'; 'authored': written for this eval. 'declined' lists what upstream has that was not adapted, with the reason.

queries.name: vEmployee
queries.adaptation: square brackets, schema prefixes and the semicolon dropped; the INNER JOIN and LEFT OUTER JOIN keywords written as JOIN and LEFT JOIN
queries.sql:
SELECT e.BusinessEntityID, p.Title, p.FirstName, p.MiddleName, p.LastName, p.Suffix, e.JobTitle, pp.PhoneNumber, pnt.Name AS PhoneNumberType, ea.EmailAddress, p.EmailPromotion,
  a.AddressLine1, a.AddressLine2, a.City, sp.Name AS StateProvinceName, a.PostalCode, cr.Name AS CountryRegionName, p.AdditionalContactInfo
FROM Employee AS e
JOIN Person AS p ON p.BusinessEntityID = e.BusinessEntityID
JOIN BusinessEntityAddress AS bea ON bea.BusinessEntityID = e.BusinessEntityID
JOIN Address AS a ON a.AddressID = bea.AddressID
JOIN StateProvince AS sp ON sp.StateProvinceID = a.StateProvinceID
JOIN CountryRegion AS cr ON cr.CountryRegionCode = sp.CountryRegionCode
LEFT JOIN PersonPhone AS pp ON pp.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID
LEFT JOIN PhoneNumberType AS pnt ON pp.PhoneNumberTypeID = pnt.PhoneNumberTypeID
LEFT JOIN EmailAddress AS ea ON p.BusinessEntityID = ea.BusinessEntityID

queries.name: vSalesPersonSalesByFiscalYears
queries.adaptation: square brackets, schema prefixes and the semicolon dropped; PIVOT (SUM([SubTotal]) FOR [FiscalYear] IN ([2002], [2003], [2004])) becomes one SUM(IF(FiscalYear = year, SubTotal, NULL)) per listed year grouped by the other columns (the same rows: PIVOT groups by every column it does not aggregate or pivot, and a year with no sales is NULL in both); '+' string concatenation becomes ||; DATEADD(m, 6, d) becomes DATETIME_ADD(d, INTERVAL 6 MONTH); YEAR() becomes EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ...). The years 2002 to 2004 are the view's own and lie outside this release's order dates (2022 to 2025), so the three columns are NULL, as they would be upstream on this data
queries.sql:
SELECT pvt.SalesPersonID, pvt.FullName, pvt.JobTitle, pvt.SalesTerritory,
  SUM(IF(pvt.FiscalYear = 2002, pvt.SubTotal, NULL)) AS `2002`, SUM(IF(pvt.FiscalYear = 2003, pvt.SubTotal, NULL)) AS `2003`, SUM(IF(pvt.FiscalYear = 2004, pvt.SubTotal, NULL)) AS `2004`
FROM (SELECT soh.SalesPersonID, p.FirstName || ' ' || COALESCE(p.MiddleName, '') || ' ' || p.LastName AS FullName, e.JobTitle, st.Name AS SalesTerritory, soh.SubTotal,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATETIME_ADD(soh.OrderDate, INTERVAL 6 MONTH)) AS FiscalYear
  FROM SalesPerson AS sp
  JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS soh ON sp.BusinessEntityID = soh.SalesPersonID
  JOIN SalesTerritory AS st ON sp.TerritoryID = st.TerritoryID
  JOIN Employee AS e ON soh.SalesPersonID = e.BusinessEntityID
  JOIN Person AS p ON p.BusinessEntityID = sp.BusinessEntityID) AS pvt
GROUP BY pvt.SalesPersonID, pvt.FullName, pvt.JobTitle, pvt.SalesTerritory

queries.adaptation: the recursive query of uspGetBillOfMaterials with @StartProductID = 749 and @CheckDate = DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00'; WITH [BOM_cte](columns) becomes WITH RECURSIVE with the names given as aliases in the anchor member (BigQuery has no column list); ISNULL becomes COALESCE; OPTION (MAXRECURSION 25) has no BigQuery form and is dropped (the recursion ends by itself on this data). BillOfMaterials dates lie in 2021 in this release while the other tables' dates are 2022 to 2025, hence the check date
queries.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE BOM_cte AS (
  SELECT b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID, p.Name AS ComponentDesc, b.PerAssemblyQty, p.StandardCost, p.ListPrice, b.BOMLevel, 0 AS RecursionLevel
  FROM BillOfMaterials AS b
  JOIN Product AS p ON b.ComponentID = p.ProductID
  WHERE b.ProductAssemblyID = 749
    AND DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' >= b.StartDate
    AND DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' <= COALESCE(b.EndDate, DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID, p.Name, b.PerAssemblyQty, p.StandardCost, p.ListPrice, b.BOMLevel, cte.RecursionLevel + 1
  FROM BOM_cte AS cte
  JOIN BillOfMaterials AS b ON b.ProductAssemblyID = cte.ComponentID
  JOIN Product AS p ON b.ComponentID = p.ProductID
  WHERE DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' >= b.StartDate
    AND DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' <= COALESCE(b.EndDate, DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00')
)
SELECT b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID, b.ComponentDesc, SUM(b.PerAssemblyQty) AS TotalQuantity, b.StandardCost, b.ListPrice, b.BOMLevel, b.RecursionLevel
FROM BOM_cte AS b
GROUP BY b.ComponentID, b.ComponentDesc, b.ProductAssemblyID, b.BOMLevel, b.RecursionLevel, b.StandardCost, b.ListPrice
ORDER BY b.BOMLevel, b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID

queries.adaptation: the recursive query of uspGetWhereUsedProductID with @StartProductID = 803 and @CheckDate = DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00'; WITH [BOM_cte](columns) becomes WITH RECURSIVE with the names given as aliases in the anchor member (BigQuery has no column list); ISNULL becomes COALESCE; OPTION (MAXRECURSION 25) has no BigQuery form and is dropped (the recursion ends by itself on this data). BillOfMaterials dates lie in 2021 in this release while the other tables' dates are 2022 to 2025, hence the check date
queries.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE BOM_cte AS (
  SELECT b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID, p.Name AS ComponentDesc, b.PerAssemblyQty, p.StandardCost, p.ListPrice, b.BOMLevel, 0 AS RecursionLevel
  FROM BillOfMaterials AS b
  JOIN Product AS p ON b.ProductAssemblyID = p.ProductID
  WHERE b.ComponentID = 803
    AND DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' >= b.StartDate
    AND DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' <= COALESCE(b.EndDate, DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID, p.Name, b.PerAssemblyQty, p.StandardCost, p.ListPrice, b.BOMLevel, cte.RecursionLevel + 1
  FROM BOM_cte AS cte
  JOIN BillOfMaterials AS b ON cte.ProductAssemblyID = b.ComponentID
  JOIN Product AS p ON b.ProductAssemblyID = p.ProductID
  WHERE DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' >= b.StartDate
    AND DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00' <= COALESCE(b.EndDate, DATETIME '2021-06-01 00:00:00')
)
SELECT b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID, b.ComponentDesc, SUM(b.PerAssemblyQty) AS TotalQuantity, b.StandardCost, b.ListPrice, b.BOMLevel, b.RecursionLevel
FROM BOM_cte AS b
GROUP BY b.ComponentID, b.ComponentDesc, b.ProductAssemblyID, b.BOMLevel, b.RecursionLevel, b.StandardCost, b.ListPrice
ORDER BY b.BOMLevel, b.ProductAssemblyID, b.ComponentID

features: scalar correlated subquery in the select list
queries.sql:

  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h WHERE h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS Orders
FROM Customer AS c
WHERE c.CustomerID BETWEEN 11000 AND 11200

JOIN SalesTerritory AS t ON h.TerritoryID = t.TerritoryID

FROM (
  SELECT CustomerID, SalesOrderID, OrderDate,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate, SalesOrderID) AS rn

FROM (
  SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, OrderQty,
    SUM(OrderQty) OVER (PARTITION BY ProductID) AS Total

JOIN Product AS p ON p.ProductID = t.ProductID

features: PIVOT as conditional sums over this release's fiscal years
queries.sql:
SELECT sp.BusinessEntityID,
  SUM(IF(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATETIME_ADD(h.OrderDate, INTERVAL 6 MONTH)) = 2023, h.SubTotal, NULL)) AS FY2023,
  SUM(IF(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATETIME_ADD(h.OrderDate, INTERVAL 6 MONTH)) = 2024, h.SubTotal, NULL)) AS FY2024,
  SUM(IF(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATETIME_ADD(h.OrderDate, INTERVAL 6 MONTH)) = 2025, h.SubTotal, NULL)) AS FY2025
FROM SalesPerson AS sp
JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON sp.BusinessEntityID = h.SalesPersonID
GROUP BY sp.BusinessEntityID

JOIN Culture AS c ON x.CultureID = c.CultureID
JOIN ProductDescription AS pd ON x.ProductDescriptionID = pd.ProductDescriptionID
WHERE c.CultureID LIKE 'en%'
